To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mammary tumours in this experimental model are not capable of degrading thyroid hormone, and that the deiodinase activities in the liver, kidney and the mammary tumorous tissue are similar to those observed in normal animals.

1) the mammary tumours are capable of generating T3 and r3T from T4; 2) the renal synthesis of T4 to T3 was significantly higher than that of T4 to r3T in tumour hosts, but no difference was observed in the hepatic T4 to T4 to rT3 and T4 to T8 conversion in tumour hosts; 3) serum T3 levels were significantly lower in tumour hosts than in controls,
the mammary tumours, the liver and the kidney of Fischer 344 rats were all capable of generating both triiodothyronine and reverse triiodothyronin...
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms involved in the generation of T3 and the possible role of this hormone in the control of tumour growth.
the role of the iodothyronines in the growth and development of the R3230 mammary tumour in Fischer 344 male rats.
the study of the regulation of thyroid hormone metabolism and its possible role in the development and/or progression of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mammary tumours studied in this investigation were capable of degrading T4 into T3, and T3 into rT3.
in the tumour and in the liver and renal tissues of tumour-bearing animals the deiodination of T4 is not different from that of normal animals.
the R3230 mammary tumours are capable of generating T3 and r3 from T4 and that the hepatic and the renal iodothyronines deiodinases are activated by the presence of the tumour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tumour does not alter iodothyronin...
the mammary tumours, liver and kidney of tumour-bearing rats were all capable of generating T3 and r3 from T4, and that the tumour did not alter the deiodination pattern of these organs.
the tumour itself does not appear to be the source of rT3 generation in this experimental tumorigenic model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mammary tumours do not seem to be able to synthesize thyroid hormones, and therefore, they do not seem to have the capacity to produce thyroid hormone-like effects.
in the tumour and in the host, the ratio of rT3 to T3 synthesis is similar to that observed in normal rats.
the R3230 mammary tumour does not have the capacity to reconvert T3 back to rT3.
